h1: Cloud consulting for New York companies on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud
intro: 22 Signals provides the cloud consulting New York companies can show their auditors, for established firms running on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud. We design the architecture, lock down access, set up monitoring and review the bill, then run it for you if you want. The result is a cloud setup your auditors can follow and your finance team can predict.

sections.h: The cloud estate most New York firms inherit
p: Few New York companies planned their cloud. It grew. A developer opened an AWS account for a product in 2016, an acquisition brought an Azure tenant, marketing runs a site on a separate host, and somewhere there is a server in a closet in a Midtown building that nobody wants to switch off. Each piece works. Together they are hard to secure, hard to audit and expensive.

For regulated firms the stakes are higher. A broker-dealer, insurer or lender licensed in the state has to show NYDFS who can reach what, how fast it would detect an incident, and how it manages its vendors. A tangled estate makes every one of those answers slower. The cloud consulting New York firms need starts with a clear map, not a migration pitch.

sections.h: NYDFS Part 500 and the SHIELD Act, in cloud terms
p: If you are licensed by the Department of Financial Services, Part 500 is the rulebook your cloud has to meet. Since November 2025 that includes multi-factor authentication for anyone accessing your information systems, a maintained asset inventory, limits on privileged access, encryption of nonpublic information, and a 72-hour window to notify the Department of a qualifying cybersecurity incident. Your cloud provider is a third-party service provider, and so are we.

Outside financial services, the SHIELD Act still applies to any business holding private information about New York residents. It asks for reasonable safeguards, and in the cloud that means encryption, access reviews, logging and a tested response plan.
We translate each control into concrete settings, apply them, and give your compliance team a document that maps the requirement to the configuration.

That work shapes how we design new setups. We assume someone will try the door, and build so that a single stolen password does not open everything.

faqs.q: Can you help us meet NYDFS Part 500 in the cloud?
faqs.a: Yes. We map each Part 500 requirement that touches your cloud, such as multi-factor authentication, access privileges, asset inventory, encryption, logging and incident response, to specific settings, apply them, and document the result. Your CISO keeps responsibility for the program and the annual filing; we give them the evidence and the working controls.

faqs.q: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud: which is best for a New York company?
faqs.a: It depends on what you already run. Firms deep in Microsoft 365 often find Azure simplest for identity and licensing. Product companies and media firms often prefer AWS for its range of services. Google Cloud is strong for data and analytics. Many clients use two. We recommend from your workloads and contracts.

faqs.q: Do you provide on-site support in New York?
faqs.a: Nearly all cloud work is done in the console and in code. For a data center visit, a hardware decommission or a workshop with your leadership, we can come to New York when the project needs it, and we will agree that in writing at the plan stage.

faqs.q: How do you cut our cloud bill without risking uptime?
faqs.a: We start with waste that carries no risk: idle resources, unattached storage, oversized test environments. Then we right-size busy systems using real usage data, move cold data to lower-cost storage tiers and buy commitments only for steady workloads. Every change has a rollback plan and is scheduled outside your busy hours.

faqs.q: What happens if something breaks in our New York systems?
faqs.a: If we manage your cloud, monitoring sends alerts to a named engineer. Response times and escalation contacts are agreed in writing at the start, and every incident gets a short written note on the cause and the fix.

faqs.q: How much does cloud consulting in New York cost?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the size of your estate, your compliance obligations, and whether you want a review, a rebuild or ongoing management. We do not publish prices. A 15-minute call is enough to tell you which of those apply and what a sensible first step would be.
